title: UAE Logistics Brief
lede: Hormuz got worse over the weekend: six tankers caught fire on Sunday and Monday after mine and projectile strikes. Iran's foreign minister is now in Muscat for talks, which are the one thing today that could ease war-risk costs.

stories.headline: Six tankers on fire in Hormuz after mine and projectile strikes
body: Six tankers caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz on Sunday and Monday, NewsNation reported. Iran's Revolutionary Guard said two oil tankers hit mines on Sunday. UKMTO said a tanker struck by an unknown projectile had an engine-room fire on Monday.

UKMTO also reported a possible mothership and skiff, with four armed people, east of Socotra off Yemen. On Monday evening 36 ships were holding position in the Hormuz area, and IMF PortWatch logged just 3 transits on 8 November against a pre-crisis 85 a day.
stories.soWhat: New since yesterday: mines are now in the story, not just drones. Expect war-risk premiums and sea freight quotes into Jebel Ali to rise again.

stories.headline: Iran's foreign minister arrives in Muscat for talks
body: Abbas Araghchi arrived in Muscat on Monday from Islamabad to meet Oman's foreign minister, Anadolu reported. The visit aims to revive the Iran-US understanding reached through Pakistani mediation.

June's 14-point Islamabad memorandum covered Hormuz maritime security, sanctions relief and an end to hostilities. Disputes over carrying it out and renewed fighting have blocked a deal, and Hormuz shipping stays restricted.
stories.soWhat: This is the event to watch today. Any agreement on Hormuz shipping would be the first real signal that surcharges can come down.

stories.headline: DP World: east-coast terminals will back up Jebel Ali, not replace it
body: DP World's GCC chief says the new Al Rugaylat and Dibba terminals in Fujairah should open within 18 to 24 months. Al Rugaylat is planned at up to 2.5 million TEUs a year; Dibba adds up to 3.6 million tonnes of general cargo.
Jebel Ali, with 19.4 million TEUs of capacity, has closed for only six hours since the war began on 28 February.
stories.soWhat: The east-coast bypass is a long-term fixture, but Jebel Ali stays the main gate. Plan freight products around both.

stories.headline: flydubai's Riyadh, Dammam and Abha ban ran to 16 November
body: flydubai cancelled all flights to Riyadh, Dammam and Abha up to and including Monday 16 November. It still flies to Jeddah, Taif, Tabuk, Medina, Al-Qassim and Ha'il.
Etihad's Riyadh and Dammam flights stay cancelled to 19 November. Emirates' booking system last showed Riyadh flights from 28 November.
stories.soWhat: The flydubai window has just ended. Check today whether it extends again; until UAE carriers return, Riyadh and Dammam freight goes by road.

competitors.name: DHL
competitors.headline: DHL Global Forwarding moves into Khor Fakkan and Fujairah
body: DHL Global Forwarding plans to build its presence in the eastern UAE, at Khor Fakkan and Dibba in Fujairah. Its €500 million Gulf investment plan is unchanged, after €120 million in the UAE and €130 million in Saudi Arabia.
DHL also has a 20-year joint venture with Etihad Rail. Its Middle East and Africa chief says logistics will take three to six months to normalise after the conflict ends.
competitors.soWhat: DHL is chasing the same east-coast bypass freight we sell. Our Khor Fakkan and Fujairah operations need a clear price and transit-time story for key accounts now.

competitors.name: FedEx
competitors.headline: US-to-Middle East demand surcharge listed at $1.50 per lb
body: FedEx's demand surcharge table, updated 5 November, lists the US to Middle East and Indian Subcontinent lane at $1.50 per lb from 6 November until further notice, after $0.75 since 24 April. The lane includes the UAE and Saudi Arabia. Minimums are $1 a parcel and $50 a freight shipment.
competitors.soWhat: US-origin express into the UAE just got dearer at FedEx. There is room to price our US inbound below them and still lift yield.

competitors.name: Aramex (baseline)
competitors.headline: Record Q3: revenue up 24%, profit up 817%
body: Q3 revenue was a record Dh1.98 billion, up 24%. Net profit rose to Dh48 million from Dh5.2 million, driven by freight forwarding. Gross margin narrowed to 21% from 23.2%.
CEO Amadou Diallo said on 2 November that freight rates may take six to 12 months to ease after peace returns, and that warehousing demand is high in the UAE, Jeddah, Turkey and India.
competitors.soWhat: Volume is up but margin is thinner. Pricing should protect gross margin on forwarding, not just chase revenue.

opportunities.title: US inbound express
opportunities.text: FedEx lists a $1.50/lb surcharge on US-to-UAE and Saudi from 6 November. A lower Aramex surcharge can win US e-commerce and B2B shippers.

opportunities.title: East-coast freight products
opportunities.text: Jebel Ali stays the main gate but Fujairah terminals are 18 to 24 months away. Sell a two-gateway product to big importers now.

opportunities.title: Riyadh and Dammam by road
opportunities.text: flydubai, Etihad and Emirates are still off Riyadh and Dammam. Keep the UAE-Saudi road service front of mind.

opportunities.title: Warehousing demand
opportunities.text: Our CEO says warehousing demand is high in the UAE and Jeddah. Push contract logistics space to shippers hit by sea delays.

watchouts.title: Mines in Hormuz
watchouts.text: Six tankers caught fire on Sunday and Monday. Sea cover and freight costs into the Gulf can jump again this week.

watchouts.title: Muscat talks could fail
watchouts.text: Araghchi is in Muscat. No deal would mean more months of restricted Hormuz shipping.

watchouts.title: DHL on the east coast
watchouts.text: DHL is building at Khor Fakkan and Fujairah with Etihad Rail behind it. Expect sharper bids on bypass freight.

watchouts.title: Thinner margins
watchouts.text: Our Q3 gross margin fell to 21% from 23.2%. High buy rates are eating into the extra revenue.

moves.title: Re-check war-risk pass-through today
moves.text: After six tanker fires, confirm sea surcharges on Jebel Ali and Khor Fakkan quotes reflect current carrier and insurer costs.

moves.title: Have two surcharge settings ready for Muscat
moves.text: Prepare a 'deal' and a 'no deal' setting so we can change rates within a day of the outcome.

moves.title: Benchmark US inbound against FedEx
moves.text: Compare our US-to-UAE and Saudi surcharge with FedEx's $1.50/lb and pitch top US-origin accounts where we are lower.

moves.title: Brief key accounts on the east-coast route
moves.text: Show Khor Fakkan and Fujairah transit times and prices before DHL's new east-coast offer reaches them.

moves.title: Confirm Saudi air status this morning
moves.text: flydubai's ban ran to 16 November. Check if it was extended and update Riyadh and Dammam service notes for customers.

moves.title: Margin floor on forwarding deals
moves.text: Set a minimum gross margin for new forwarding quotes so revenue growth does not keep pulling margin down.
